newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar closes firmer in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar closes firmer in quiet trading.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar nudged slightly higher at the close after a quiet day's trading on Thursday.
"It has been a fairly quiet day with a slow and gradual move up," one bank dealer said.
The currency opened at US$0.6923/30 and closed at 0.6929/36 in what was a "non-event day" the dealer said.
On the Trade-Weighted Index the kiwi opened at 65.54 and closed at 65.66.
"We have seen more of the type of activity of the past few weeks, with investor flows dominating. But it is very quiet domestically," the dealer said.
Dealers said overnight trading had been quiet for the past few days so they expected a range of 0.6925-0.6940 tonight.

Longer term, the focus now moved to U.S. non-farm payroll numbers due out on Friday and to the pre-election economic and fiscal update on September 12 and the Reserve Bank's economic forecasts on September 13.
"Before then maybe we can edge up and have another look at 0.6950," the dealer said. -- Vernon Small 64 4 4714 278
